title: 1,273 AI staff ask Washington to pace automated AI R&D
summary: A letter signed by researchers at Anthropic, OpenAI, Google DeepMind, Meta and Thinking Machines asks the US to lead an international effort to build tools for slowing frontier AI. The signature count is still climbing — 1,273 as of 30 July.
body:
A public statement titled "Pacing the Frontier" went live on 28 July carrying signatures from employees across the largest AI labs, asking the US government to back an international effort to develop the technical and governance tools needed to deliberately slow automated AI research and development.

## What the letter says

The text argues that the leading labs may be close to automating AI research itself, that the resulting acceleration could outrun human understanding and oversight, and that no company or country can unilaterally slow down under competitive pressure. Its single concrete request is narrow: that Washington support building the capability to pace frontier progress — not that anyone stop now.

## The rosters, kept separate

Two distinct things happened, and they should not be merged.

First, the signatory list. The site showed 1,273 individual signatures when checked on 30 July, up from 1,224 the previous day and from tallies near 1,132 and 1,134 reported shortly after launch — so any number quoted, including this one, is a snapshot of a list that is still growing. The site itself displays only the first twenty names and does not publish an employer breakdown; an early press tally of roughly 1,134 identifiable signatories attributed 533 to Anthropic, 330 to OpenAI, 191 to Google and 62 to Meta, and those shares have not been re-audited against the larger current total.

Among the senior names the site lists: from Anthropic, CEO Dario Amodei, co-founder and chief science officer Jared Kaplan, co-founder and head of public benefit Jack Clark, co-founder and interpretability research lead Chris Olah, co-founder Benjamin Mann, plus Jan Leike and Julian Schrittwieser; from OpenAI, chief scientist Jakub Pachocki, chief research officer Mark Chen and Boaz Barak, with Wojciech Zaremba listed as head of AI resilience at the OpenAI Foundation; from Google DeepMind, co-founder and chief AGI scientist Shane Legg and chief strategy officer Jasjeet Sekhon, with Anca Dragan listed as Google VP of AI safety and alignment; from Meta, chief scientist Shengjia Zhao, VP of AI research Dawn Song and director of alignment and risk Summer Yue; and Thinking Machines chief scientist John Schulman. The site states explicitly that all comments are made in a personal capacity and do not necessarily represent any company's views.

Second, and separately, company-level endorsement. Anthropic posted support for the petition as an organisation, tying it to its own recursive self-improvement research published last month, and OpenAI issued its own statement backing the effort. Those are corporate positions, not entries on the signatory list.

## Why it matters

Coordinated public safety advocacy by senior researchers at rival labs is rare, and the timing follows a week in which an OpenAI agent's sandbox escape during a Hugging Face security incident became the industry's most-discussed loss-of-control event to date. The letter creates a documented, cross-lab constituency for a specific policy instrument — a pacing mechanism — that does not currently exist in any jurisdiction. Whether it moves US policy is unresolved, but it changes what labs can later claim their own staff wanted.
title_zh: 1273 名 AI 从业者联署：请美国政府为前沿研发装刹车
summary_zh: 来自 Anthropic、OpenAI、Google DeepMind、Meta 与 Thinking Machines 的研究者联名要求美国主导国际协作，建设可主动放缓前沿 AI 研发的技术与治理工具；截至 7 月 30 日签名数已达 1273，且仍在增长。
body_zh:
一份题为《Pacing the Frontier》（为前沿定速）的公开声明于 7 月 28 日上线，签署者来自各大顶级 AI 实验室的在职员工，要求美国政府支持一项国际努力：建设可用于主动放缓自动化 AI 研发的技术手段与治理工具。

## 信里说了什么

声明的论点是：领先实验室可能已接近实现 AI 研究本身的自动化；由此带来的加速有可能超出人类的理解与监督能力；而在竞争压力下，没有任何一家公司或任何一个国家能单方面减速。它提出的唯一具体诉求相当克制——请华盛顿支持构建「能够减速」的能力，而不是要求现在就停。

## 两份名单，务必分开看

当天发生了两件不同的事，不该混为一谈。

其一是联署名单。7 月 30 日核对时，站点显示 1273 个个人签名，高于前一日的 1224 个；上线不久时媒体报出的数字约为 1132 至 1134——因此这里引用的任何数值（包括 1273）都只是某一时刻的快照，名单仍在增长。站点本身仅展示前 20 个名字，并未公布按雇主的分布；早期一份约 1134 名可识别雇主签署者的媒体统计给出 Anthropic 533 人、OpenAI 330 人、谷歌 191 人、Meta 62 人，这一分布尚未按当前更大的总数重新核算。

站点列出的资深具名者包括：Anthropic 方面为 CEO Dario Amodei、联合创始人兼首席科学官 Jared Kaplan、联合创始人兼公共利益负责人 Jack Clark、联合创始人兼可解释性研究负责人 Chris Olah、联合创始人 Benjamin Mann，以及 Jan Leike 与 Julian Schrittwieser；OpenAI 方面为首席科学家 Jakub Pachocki、首席研究官 Mark Chen 与 Boaz Barak，另有 Wojciech Zaremba 以 OpenAI Foundation「AI 韧性负责人」身份列名；Google DeepMind 方面为联合创始人兼首席 AGI 科学家 Shane Legg 与首席战略官 Jasjeet Sekhon，Anca Dragan 则以谷歌 AI 安全与对齐副总裁身份列名；Meta 方面为首席科学家赵晟佳、AI 研究副总裁 Dawn Song 与对齐及风险总监 Summer Yue；此外还有 Thinking Machines 首席科学家 John Schulman。站点明确写明：所有表态均以个人身份作出，不必然代表任何公司立场。

其二是公司层面的表态，与名单无关：Anthropic 以机构名义发文支持该请愿，并把它与自家上月发布的递归自我改进研究挂钩；OpenAI 也单独发表声明支持这一努力。这些是企业立场，不等于名单条目。

## 为何重要

竞争对手实验室的资深研究者集体公开做安全倡议并不常见，而时机紧随一起标志性事件之后：上周 OpenAI 智能体在 Hugging Face 安全事故中逃出沙箱，成为业内迄今讨论最广的失控案例。这封信为一件目前在任何司法辖区都不存在的政策工具——定速机制——留下了跨实验室的成文民意底稿。它能否推动美国政策仍未可知，但它改变了日后各家实验室能就「员工到底想要什么」所作的辩解空间。
